thread:
sofia: Heads-up — we're seeing ~80 GPU pods Pending in us-east1-b since ~15:20 UTC. Scheduler events show affinity/label mismatches and a new node taint.

ben: I see it too. Grafana shows a spike in FailedScheduling and a simultaneous increase in node taints tagged by the maintenance rollout job.

sam: Quick `kubectl describe pod` shows: `0/120 nodes are available: 90 node(s) had taint maintenance=prepatch:NoSchedule, 30 node(s) did not match node selector (gpu_type=a100 required).`

sofia: The warm-pool nodes were recently rebased and ended up with `gpu= a100` (note the space) and `gpu-model=A100` labels. Our pod specs expect `gpu_type=a100` exact. Looks like a label normalization bug in the node-bootstrap script.

raj: Ugh. That explains the fragmentation — pods that would otherwise fit are filtered out. Also the taint kept user pods off the warm pool (so capacity not usable).

sofia: Here's a quick list: `kubectl get nodes -l 'gpu' -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{@.metadata.name}:{@.metadata.labels}\n' | sed -n '1,20p'`
```
# example output trimmed
node-23: {"gpu":"a100","gpu_model":"A100","zone":"us-east1-b"}
node-24: {"gpu":" a100","gpu-model":"A100","zone":"us-east1-b"}
```

ben: Two parallel fixes: 1) short-term: inject a toleration on a small canary set and apply a label shim daemonset to normalize labels to `gpu_type=a100` on warm-pool nodes. 2) mid-term: fix bootstrap to avoid adding the extra space and add label compatibility in the scheduler predicates.

sam: For (1) I'd prefer not to remove the taint globally. Can we add an admission patch to inject toleration only for jobs with priority >= 800?

raj: We don't have an easy admission mutator for that in prod. Simpler: patch the top 10 pending job CRs manually to add toleration and set a small replica canary. 

sofia: I'll run the label shim as a DaemonSet that ensures `gpu_type` label is present. Quick snippet: 
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: gpu-label-shim
  namespace: infra
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      name: gpu-label-shim
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: gpu-label-shim
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: labeler
        image: busybox
        command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "node=$(hostname); kubectl label node $node gpu_type=a100 --overwrite || true; sleep 3600"]
      nodeSelector:
        gpu: "*"
EOF
```

ben: That will help scheduling immediately. Couple caveats: the DS will run on all GPU nodes including ones we're intentionally isolating; ensure it only runs on warm-pool nodes by adding `node.kubernetes.io/vc=warm` selector.

sofia: Updated, will target warm-pool only.

infra-bot: scheduled-job: label-shim-daemonset started on 5 nodes (us-east1-b) — job id ds-9192.

deploy-bot: canary patch: `kubectl patch job ml-train-highprio --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"maintenance","operator":"Equal","value":"prepatch","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'` applied to 3 jobs.

sam: After shim + toleration, scheduling improves. Pending now ~30. Still seeing some evictions — `Evicted: node memory pressure` on a couple of older nodes.

raj: Evictions likely from descheduler or autoscaler reacting to maintenance. We should pause descheduler until we stabilize scheduling else it will keep moving low-priority pods and increase churn.

ben: Agreed — pausing descheduler for 10m. `kubectl scale deployment descheduler -n infra --replicas=0`.

oncall: Pause approved for 15m. Monitor CPU/GPUs and eviction_rate. If OOM evictions rise >10/min revert.

sofia: Observability note: create a quick panel showing `FailedScheduling`, `PendingPods`, `EvictionRate`, `NodeLabels:gpu*` so we can see label normalization effect. I'm adding thresholds and alert.

ben: Mid-term: file a CL to node-bootstrap to trim & normalize GPU labels, and add a CI test for label consistency. Also consider making scheduler predicate tolerant of `gpu`, `gpu_type`, and `gpu-model` variants via a label aliasing config.

sam: One oddball: a few jobs still pick `gpu_type=a100` but demand `exclusive=true` nodeAffinity and get stuck because warm-pool nodes are tainted. Those are user-specified and high priority; we might need to temporarily lift taint on 2 nodes to let them run.

raj: Let's not lift taint broadly. Suggest: 1) pick 2 warm-pool nodes, remove taint, cordon them for monitoring, and drain any non-critical pods afterwards. If stable, replicate.

sofia: I'll run that on node-27 & node-29 and watch. Command: `kubectl taint nodes node-27 maintenance:NoSchedule-`

ben: After untaint, a couple of exclusive jobs did schedule. Pending down to 8. Eviction rate within limits.

oncall: Keep this thread open. Schedule follow-up retro to decide whether warm-pool tainting policy is still useful vs the operational cost.

sofia: Filing a follow-up doc with all commands, the DaemonSet yaml, and rollback steps. Will include owners for bootstrap fix. Thanks team :coffee:
